risks.note: Sugarcane is the main raw material and is monsoon dependent. Climate variation cut Tamil Nadu cane availability from 123 lakh tons to 84 lakh tons and the company's own crushing fell to 11.29 lakh tons from 12.29 lakh tons. The MD&A notes intense summer in H1 2024 and Cyclone Fengal in November 2024 depressed planting, with a 12-month gestation lag that carried the shortfall into January-March 2026. Scarcity of harvest labour and the availability of attractive competing crops with remunerative prices compound the risk.
risks.risk: Sugarcane availability — climate-dependent and structurally shrinking in Tamil Nadu

risks.note: The Board perceives the risk of recurring lower sugar recovery in Tamil Nadu compared with the minimum recovery at which mills must pay the Fair and Remunerative Price. TN mills must pay FRP at 9.50% irrespective of actual recovery — paying for 95 kg of sugar equivalent while recovering only 81.5 kg. The gap between FRP payable and RSF value is Rs 321 per ton of cane which mills are unable to recover, and 'the loss works out to Rs 535 per ton of cane crushed'.
risks.risk: Sugar recovery below the FRP peg — a structural loss per ton of cane in Tamil Nadu

risks.note: 'The capacity utilization is around 33% which has resulted in the sub-optimal production of sugar, power and alcohol. Accordingly, the incidence of fixed cost has more than tripled compared to normal times, leaving correspondingly lower amount in the hands of mills for cane payment.' The Board separately records that lower capacity utilisation is a concern.
risks.risk: Low capacity utilisation and fixed-cost absorption

risks.note: The Company has been under a monitoring period since the debt restructuring implemented by lenders with retrospective effect from 30.06.2020, is operating without working capital facilities from the consortium lenders, and has to continuously sell inventory to maintain cash flows; this will continue until its account is upgraded as standard. The sugar industry is highly working capital intensive and management flags that raising adequate and rightly-priced working capital for peak-period operation might pose a challenge. Mitigation is the restructuring's beneficial terms (reduced interest rate, deferred repayment) plus a Rs 30 crore Dropline Overdraft repayable over 21 months and a Rs 20 crore Cash Credit from Kotak Mahindra Bank.
risks.risk: Financial liquidity — operating without consortium working capital while under lender monitoring

risks.note: The industry is regulated on cane area reservation, cane price fixation, the monthly sugar release mechanism, an MSP of Rs 31/kg, and export quotas. The Company challenged the monthly sugar release mechanism in court; the Madras High Court dismissed its writ petition and the Company filed a writ appeal on 24.10.2024, which is pending disposal. The Board notes Government policy on sugar will continue to have a significant bearing on the prospects of the industry.
risks.risk: Government regulation of sugar pricing and release — including litigation the company has lost at first instance

risks.note: The Tamil Nadu government has been allowing IMFL manufacturers to import a major share of their Extra Neutral Alcohol requirement from neighbouring states at comparatively lower tax rates, giving other states an unfair advantage and adversely affecting the cash flow stream of TN sugar manufacturers, since ENA is one of the main revenue streams. Tamil Nadu's option to shift into ethanol is also limited by restricted molasses availability.
risks.risk: Distillery / ENA revenue displaced by inter-state imports into Tamil Nadu

risks.note: Price realisation is one of the industry's major risks, though management judges the perceived risk 'lower given the outlook of lower stock available'. Mitigation is structural — downstream alcohol and cogeneration using molasses and bagasse to complement profitability, added flexibility to make ethanol from cane juice/syrup, and selling sugar regularly at every price point to improve average realisation.

'The unpredictable climate variations, rainfall pattern & low recovery are threats to the sustainable operation of the Industry. International weather pattern suggests that this year would be a worst El Nino Year in the last 140 years.' The company mitigates with drip irrigation, water gel application, trash shredding/mulching, focus on areas with better ground water availability and drought-tolerant varietal work.
